fields.System.Title: INT-204 — Retry and dead-letter failed deliveries
fields.System.Description:
Story

As a developer, I want outbound delivery failures handled predictably, so that a
consumer outage resolves itself and a poisoned event does not block everything behind it.

Acceptance criteria

  • - Given a delivery failure, then it is retried with increasing delay, as in
  • [FDN-803](../FDN/FDN-803-retry-with-backoff.md).
  • - Given the consumer recovers, then queued events deliver in the correct order per
  • aggregate.
  • - Given an event failing beyond the retry limit, then it dead-letters and alerts a
  • person.
  • - Given a dead-lettered event, then events for other aggregates continue to deliver.
  • - Given the outbox backlog exceeding an age threshold, then an alert is raised — a
  • silent backlog looks exactly like a healthy queue.
  • - Given a fixed problem, then a dead-lettered event can be replayed.

Traceability

| Aspect | Detail |
|---|---|
| Modules | platform |
| Tables | outbox |
| Risks | Poisoned event blocking the queue; backlog nobody notices ([doc 08 §9](../../../docs/08-data-sync-and-migrations.md)) |
| Tests | integration |
